text: Spillover or not, the effect on the Chadian side is the same for families near the line. I'd separate intent from impact here.
Fair point on fuel, but repeated strikes near the border don't fit a simple supply dispute.
Agree on bursts. Dry season movement could pull the timing forward, though.
Amdjarass is the one I'd watch too. A strike there would hit aid flights as well as the headlines.
Same pattern elsewhere in the Sahel. Access took far longer to come back than the fighting took to move on.
Worth checking with partners in Adré first. Some tracks may still be cut after the last storms.
We hear the same on the Chad side. Rumours about registration can move people as fast as shelling does.
